main_body: Two-storey half-timbered tavern: a large terracotta tile roof (rows 0-43) over a plaster front wall (rows 44-95) with timber frame, shuttered windows, a plank door and a hanging beer sign
top_band: Orange terracotta tile roof slope, rows 0-43, with lighter tile highlights and a darker brown eave line at rows 42-44
evidence: In the middle column, the tiled roof slope appears as a tall band of staggered tile rows with highlights (rows 0-41). It ends in a distinct eave edge with a dark brown shadow row directly below (about rows 42-45). Below that is the vertical plaster face (rows 46-90) with timber posts and beams and a stone base. The door has a dark inset frame with a lintel, and the windows have shutters and sills. The roof clearly reads as the top surface above the front face, matching the reference houses. No receding side faces.

style.evidence: The roof has per-tile highlights and shadows in about 5 orange-brown steps. The plaster has speckled grey-cream variation. The timber is dark brown, with tinted outlines and no black sticker line. The door planks, shutters and stone base all carry shading. Tile detail is as rich as the references or richer, with no large flat fills.
